summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status skipped; simulation_allowed false) because the custom experiment has no blocks and no power_w object, so input validity failed. The deterministic gate sets comparison_valid to false and input_gate_pass and scientific_gate_pass to false. The scenario is the Figure 10 FP1 vs FP2 comparison of 4-layer 3D floorplans of the GSRC n100 benchmark. The only published numbers are FP1 area 0.319 mm2 with HotSpot peak 564 K, FP2 area 0.326 mm2 with peak 567 K, a random power-density range of 1e5-1e7 W/m2, and a 45 nm node assumption. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so it is a steady run with no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes and powers were supplied. No illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated, so there is no source commit or generated-placement assumption to report. No Studio temperature exists. The 564 K and 567 K values are HotSpot steady-state peak temperatures over a 4-layer stack with a top heat sink, and they cannot be matched numerically to any 2D result. Any future 2D run would differ in location (3D stack peak, layer 0 hottest, vs single layer), aggregation, vertical conduction, TSV treatment, and package and boundary assumptions. At most one could discuss qualitative sensitivity, for example that a slightly larger area FP2 had a slightly higher peak than FP1. This is not exact replication, and no thermal conclusion is drawn from Studio for this paper.

The scenario is a 4-layer TSV-based 3D IC with vertical heat conduction through the active Si, BEOL SiO2 and TIM layers. A 2D, single-layer Studio model cannot represent inter-layer heat transfer, TSV islands (treated as zero-power modules), or layer 0 being farthest from the heat sink.

The original thermal metric is a power-based TGV (a sum of 2x2 sub-grid power densities adjusted for neighbor cells) alongside HotSpot peak temperature. It is not a finite-difference temperature solution, so the Studio solver cannot reproduce the paper's TGV or its HotSpot-vs-TGV correlation and success-rate analysis.

The paper's optimizer is an evolutionary 3D floorplanner generating many floorplans, and its goal is ranking floorplan pairs, not optimizing a single design. The selected FP1/FP2 comparison involves no controller, transient behaviour or reliability analysis, so any Studio optimizer or controller is not part of the original experiment.

Module coordinates, dimensions and powers for FP1/FP2 are not published. Power densities were randomly assigned (1e5-1e7 W/m2) and no per-module watts exist, so a faithful geometry and power input cannot be built. Cooling is described only as a heat sink on top, with no HotSpot package parameters beyond 'default'.
No complete experiment is reproducible. The floorplan must stay empty (no paper-derived blocks, coordinates or power_rows). Total chip power is not split among modules.
Any bundled Studio package, material and cooling assumptions are Studio-side. They are not taken from the paper and are not equivalent to the HotSpot default 3D stack with a top-mounted heat sink.

If a runner builds a separate illustrative 2D placement and one-row power trace from dimensions and powers, its generated coordinates are distinct from paper facts. Its temperatures must not be compared numerically to 564 K or 567 K.
The paper's only published numeric facts for this scenario are the FP1/FP2 areas and HotSpot peak temperatures (pdf page 6), and no complete set of geometry, power and boundary data accompanies them.
